C1:
Two problems. (1) Humanoid:MoveTo times out: if the goal isn't reached in ~8 seconds, MoveToFinished fires anyway with reached=false. You ignore that argument, so it prints "arrived". (2) MoveTo walks in a straight line with no pathfinding, so it hits walls. Fix: use PathfindingService and walk the waypoints, checking the reached flag. Also set network ownership to the server so the walking doesn't stutter.
```lua
local PFS = game:GetService("PathfindingService")
local hum = zombie.Humanoid
local path = PFS:CreatePath({AgentRadius=2, AgentHeight=5, AgentCanJump=true})
local ok = pcall(function() path:ComputeAsync(zombie.PrimaryPart.Position, target.Position) end)
if ok and path.Status == Enum.PathStatus.Success then
  for _, wp in path:GetWaypoints() do
    if wp.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump then hum.Jump = true end
    hum:MoveTo(wp.Position)
    if not hum.MoveToFinished:Wait() then break end -- stuck or timed out, so recompute
  end
end
```
Listen to path.Blocked and recompute. Re-path every so often while the target moves. If one MoveTo has to run longer than 8 seconds, call it again before the timeout runs out.
C2: ScreenGui.ResetOnSpawn defaults to true. On every respawn the ScreenGui in PlayerGui is destroyed and a fresh copy is cloned from StarterGui. The LocalScript inside it restarts too, so its local variables go back to their defaults. Fix: set ResetOnSpawn = false on that ScreenGui so it and its script survive respawns. Another option is to keep the state outside the GUI, for example in a ModuleScript or a LocalScript in StarterPlayerScripts, or in attributes on the Player, and rebuild the UI from it. If the settings must persist across sessions, save them on the server in a DataStore through a remote. Also, code that holds references to the character must re-fetch them on CharacterAdded.
C3: Animation replication works through the Animator. Animations played from the client replicate only when the client has authority over that Animator: its own character, since it owns the character's network physics. A server-owned NPC isn't controlled by your client, so an animation you play on it stays local and only you see it. An Animator created with Instance.new on the client exists only on that client, so nothing replicates from it. Fix: play NPC animations from a server Script (Humanoid/AnimationController -> Animator:LoadAnimation(anim):Play()). Have the server create the Animator, or let the Humanoid create it. If the client triggers the wave, fire a RemoteEvent and have the server validate it and play the animation. Alternatively, have every client play it locally, for example by firing all clients. Keep playing the player's own character animations on the client: that is correct and they replicate. Never create Animators on the client for things that must replicate.
C4: (1) A Sound whose parent is not a BasePart or Attachment (for example Workspace or SoundService) is non-positional (2D). Every listener hears it at full volume everywhere. Fix: parent it to a Part or Attachment at the barrel. (2) Positional sounds attenuate between RollOffMinDistance and RollOffMaxDistance (and by RollOffMode). Fix: raise RollOffMaxDistance (and RollOffMinDistance), or use RollOffMode InverseTapered/Linear. You can also add volume, but check Volume limits. (3) Loaded fires only once, when loading finishes. If the sound was already loaded before you connected, Wait() hangs forever. Asset failures or moderation also stop it from ever firing. Fix: `if not siren.IsLoaded then siren.Loaded:Wait() end`, ideally with a timeout. Or just call :Play(), which plays once the sound has loaded. ContentProvider:PreloadAsync can also preload it.
C5:
workspace:Raycast(origin, direction): direction is a displacement, so its length is the ray length. A .Unit vector casts only 1 stud, so it usually hits nothing and returns nil. Indexing nil errors. Also, the ray starts inside your own character, so it hits your own body unless you exclude it.
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {player.Character}
local origin = head.Position
local dir = (mouseHit - origin).Unit * 500
local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if result then
  print(result.Instance.Name, result.Position)
end
```
Always nil-check the result. Use mouse.UnitRay/camera rays as needed. For a real gun, send the hit info to the server and validate it there with a server raycast; never trust client damage.
C6:
Two tweens on the same property of the same instance conflict. When a new tween starts on BackgroundTransparency, Roblox cancels the earlier tween on that property. The hover tween stops partway, and the click tween's 'back' value is taken from a snapshot of the half-finished state. Unordered MouseLeave/MouseEnter events then leave the button in odd states. Structure it as a small state machine with one owner per property: track state (hovered, pressed) and one current tween; cancel it before starting another, and always tween to the target computed from the state, not to relative or snapshot values.
```lua
local current
local hovered = false
local function goTo(t, time)
  if current then current:Cancel() end
  current = TweenService:Create(btn, TweenInfo.new(time), {BackgroundTransparency = t})
  current:Play()
end
btn.MouseEnter:Connect(function() hovered = true; goTo(0.2, 0.3) end)
btn.MouseLeave:Connect(function() hovered = false; goTo(0.5, 0.3) end)
btn.Activated:Connect(function()
  goTo(0, 0.05)
  current.Completed:Wait()
  goTo(hovered and 0.2 or 0.5, 0.15)
end)
```
Or animate the flash on a different property or object (for example a UIStroke or an overlay frame) so the two effects never compete.

```lua
local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local conns = {}
local function onAdded(part)
  if not part:IsA("BasePart") or conns[part] then return end
  conns[part] = part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
    local char = hit:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
    local hum = char and char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if hum and Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(char) and hum.Health > 0 then
      hum.Health = 0
    end
  end)
end
local function onRemoved(part)
  if conns[part] then conns[part]:Disconnect(); conns[part] = nil end
end
CollectionService:GetInstanceAddedSignal("Lava"):Connect(onAdded)
CollectionService:GetInstanceRemovedSignal("Lava"):Connect(onRemoved)
for _, p in CollectionService:GetTagged("Lava") do onAdded(p) end
```
Rules: run it on the server (a Script in ServerScriptService), so the kill is authoritative. Connect the Added/Removed signals AND loop over the existing GetTagged parts so nothing is missed. The removed signal also fires when a tagged instance leaves the DataModel (is destroyed), so a table keyed by part plus Disconnect avoids leaks. Guard against non-parts and duplicate connections. CanTouch must be true.

```lua
local MPS = game:GetService("MarketplaceService")
local DSS = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local store = DSS:GetDataStore("PlayerData")
local PRODUCT_ID = 123456
MPS.ProcessReceipt = function(info)
  if info.ProductId ~= PRODUCT_ID then return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  local key = "Player_" .. info.PlayerId
  local ok, err = pcall(function()
    store:UpdateAsync(key, function(data)
      data = data or {Coins = 0, Receipts = {}}
      data.Receipts = data.Receipts or {}
      if data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] then return data end -- already granted
      data.Coins += 500
      data.Receipts[info.PurchaseId] = true
      return data
    end)
  end)
  if not ok then warn(err); return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.NotProcessedYet end
  -- update the in-memory/leaderstats value if the player is online
  return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted
end
```
Rules: assign ProcessReceipt only once, in one server Script. Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant is durably saved. On any failure, or an unknown product or player, return NotProcessedYet; Roblox retries later, including when the player rejoins. Make it idempotent by recording PurchaseId in the same atomic UpdateAsync as the coins, so retries never double-grant. Don't yield forever and don't error (wrap in pcall). If you use session-locked profile data, write to the profile and save it before returning Granted. Trim old receipt IDs.

Store the raw text if you need it, but filter again whenever you redisplay it (for example after a reload, or in a later session, when the author may be offline; you can still filter with their UserId). C10:
```lua
local DSS = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local store = DSS:GetDataStore("PlayerData")
local function addGems(player, amount)
  assert(typeof(amount) == "number" and amount == amount and amount > 0)
  local key = "Player_" .. player.UserId
  for attempt = 1, 3 do
    local ok, result = pcall(function()
      return store:UpdateAsync(key, function(old)
        old = old or {Gems = 0}
        old.Gems = (old.Gems or 0) + amount
        return old
      end)
    end)
    if ok then return true, result.Gems end
    warn("addGems failed:", result)
    task.wait(2 ^ attempt)
  end
  return false
end
```
Rules: the callback may run more than once, so it must be pure. It may not yield (no waits or other DataStore calls) and must have no side effects such as granting items or firing remotes. Do those only after UpdateAsync succeeds. Return nil to cancel the write. Handle a nil old value (a new player). Return only serializable data (no Instances or mixed tables), under 4 MB. Wrap the call in pcall, retry with backoff, and respect the request budget (GetRequestBudgetForRequestType). Run it on the server only, and validate the amount there.

C13: Use MemoryStoreService, not DataStores. DataStores are slow and persistent, have strict write throttles (one write per key every ~6 s) and no queue semantics, and stale entries never expire. Use MemoryStoreService:GetQueue (MemoryStoreQueue: AddAsync with an expiration and priority, then ReadAsync with an invisibility timeout and RemoveAsync to acknowledge), or a MemoryStoreSortedMap keyed by skill/MMR bucket for skill-based lookups. Design: lobby servers add players with a short TTL (refreshed while they wait). A single matchmaker (elected through a lock in a sorted map, or rotated) reads a batch, groups players by skill window (widening over time), reserves a server with TeleportService:ReserveServer, and publishes the match. Use MessagingService, or a per-player map entry, to tell lobby servers which players to teleport. Then RemoveAsync the read items; if the matchmaker crashes, the invisibility timeout returns them to the queue. Limits: memory quota of about 64 KB + 1 KB x users (per experience, now with larger per-experience pools); request units of about 1000 + 100 x users per minute; items up to 32 KB; max TTL 45 days; partitions per structure have throughput caps, so shard hot queues. Everything is ephemeral and can fail, so pcall with retries, handle players who left or already matched, and expect at-least-once processing (make it idempotent).
C14: Flow: in the lobby server, TeleportService:ReserveServer(matchPlaceId) returns an access code. Then call TeleportService:TeleportAsync(matchPlaceId, {p1,p2,p3,p4}, options) with a TeleportOptions where ReservedServerAccessCode = code (or ShouldReserveServer = true). Teleport data: TeleportOptions:SetTeleportData({matchId=...}) is sent through the client and can be tampered with, so use it only for non-sensitive hints. For the loadout and coins, read authoritative data on the match server: load each player's DataStore/profile on PlayerAdded (the same experience shares DataStores). Or write a match record (memberIds, loadouts) to MemoryStore keyed by matchId/access code before teleporting, and have the match server read it; it knows its PrivateServerId/reserved code. Pitfalls: TeleportAsync must be called from the server, and it yields and can fail (pcall, retry with backoff, handle TeleportInitFailed). Make sure the lobby has saved the player's data and released the session lock before the teleport, or the match server reads stale data or double-loads (use session locking). Teleport data isn't trusted and the coin balance must come from the server's store. Some players may fail or arrive late, so use a timeout and handle partial parties. Validate on the match server that arriving players belong to the match. Reserved servers can't be joined through friends. Teleports don't work in Studio.
C15: Never trust the client for prices, ownership or currency. The client only sends intent: BuyItem:FireServer("Sword") (or an item ID); better, a RemoteFunction that returns the result. The server: (1) validates argument types and that the item exists in a server-side catalog (a ModuleScript in ServerStorage or a shared read-only config); (2) looks up the price itself; (3) checks the player's server-held balance, level/requirements, and whether they already own the item; (4) atomically deducts and grants in the server data/profile, then saves; (5) rate-limits and debounces each player to stop double-buy races; (6) returns success or failure, which the UI shows. The client UI may display prices from a replicated config, but that is cosmetic only. Leaderstats and currency values are written only by the server, and the server ignores any numbers the client sends. Robux items use MarketplaceService with ProcessReceipt, not remotes. Log suspicious requests.
C16: Use Roblox localization with a LocalizationTable for the experience (the cloud translation table in Creator Hub, with auto-text-capture for static UI). Let automatic translation or translators fill in es, pt and de. Runtime strings: don't concatenate translated fragments. Define keyed entries with parameters, for example key "QuestCollected" with source "You collected {1} of {2} {3}", or named parameters {count}/{total}. On the client: `local translator = LocalizationService:GetTranslatorForPlayerAsync(player)` (in pcall), then `label.Text = translator:FormatByKey("QuestCollected", {count, total, itemName})`. Translate the item name through its own key, and handle plurals with separate keys. Set AutoLocalize = false on labels you fill this way, or because they are already localized, so auto-translate doesn't double-process them. NPC names: set AutoLocalize = false on the name labels (BillboardGuis) and keep them out of the table, or mark them as don't-translate entries. Use the player's locale (Player.LocaleId / translator.LocaleId), and re-render when it changes. Keep the server sending keys and arguments, not prebuilt English sentences. Test with the Studio locale emulator, and leave room for longer German text (TextScaled or auto-size).
C17: Yes, for the continuous state. UnreliableRemoteEvent sends unordered, unacknowledged packets: no resend on loss and no ordering guarantee. That suits high-frequency, superseding data such as steering/throttle snapshots and cosmetic exhaust effects, because a dropped packet is simply replaced by the next one and nothing queues up behind it (lower latency). Rules: use it only for data where loss is acceptable and the newest value wins. Keep the payload small: each event must fit in about 900 bytes, and oversized events are dropped. Include a timestamp or sequence number and ignore stale or out-of-order packets; interpolate on the receiver. It only has FireServer/FireClient/FireAllClients plus OnServerEvent/OnClientEvent, with no return values. Server validation still applies. Lap completions, finishes, purchases and any state change that must arrive go on a normal reliable RemoteEvent. Also consider whether car physics already replicate through network ownership; then you only need inputs or effects, not 20 Hz positions. Send only to relevant (nearby) clients, and quantize values (buffers) to cut bandwidth.
C18: Unanchored parts near players get automatic network ownership: the engine hands physics simulation to the nearest player's client. When players approach, ownership of the boss switches between server and clients, which causes stutter or teleport hitches. The owning client also simulates the boss, so an exploiter can move it, and touches are reported from their simulation, so Touched-based damage can be faked or triggered at will. Fix: call boss.PrimaryPart:SetNetworkOwner(nil) (on all assemblies of the boss) on the server after spawning, so the server always simulates it. Check that it isn't anchored first, and note that automatic ownership is then off for that assembly. Do damage on the server: use spatial queries (GetPartBoundsInBox or GetPartsInPart, or a magnitude check) at attack frames or on a server timer, with cooldowns per target, instead of trusting client-driven Touched. Validate distance and line of sight on the server. For many NPCs, consider server-side movement with lightweight physics (or anchored and CFrame-driven with client-side interpolation) to reduce cost.
C19: Structure: put each group of turrets under an Actor (for example 60 turrets in roughly 4-8 Actors, or one per turret). The script inside the Actor connects with ConnectParallel to RunService.Heartbeat (or calls task.desynchronize()), then reads state and runs workspace:Raycast for its turrets in parallel. It stores results in local tables. Then task.synchronize() (or a later serial phase) applies the effects: rotating the turret, firing, damage, remotes. Use Actor:SendMessage/BindToMessage to pass targets in. SharedTable can share read-mostly data between Actors. Restrictions: in a desynchronized (parallel) phase you can read most properties and call thread-safe APIs (Raycast, GetPartBoundsInBox and similar spatial queries are safe), but you cannot write properties of instances outside your Actor, create or destroy instances, fire remotes, or call unsafe APIs; switch to serial for that. Each Actor has its own Lua VM, so modules are required separately per Actor and globals/state are not shared. Use SharedTable or messages instead. Parallel work only pays off when there is enough work to split. Reduce work as well: run line-of-sight at 5-10 Hz per turret staggered across frames, cull by distance first, and reuse RaycastParams. Profile with the MicroProfiler to confirm the speedup.
C20: Before a server teleport, call player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(targetPosition, timeout) (server-side, in pcall) so the area around the destination streams in on that client first. Then PivotTo. Optionally freeze the character briefly (anchor the HumanoidRootPart) and wait for the floor on the client before releasing it. Set Workspace.StreamingIntegrityMode to PauseOutsideLoadedArea (or MinimumRadiusPause) so the player's physics pause until the area around them has loaded, instead of falling through. Mark important models (the dungeon entrance, floor or map) with ModelStreamingMode = Atomic/Persistent; use Persistent sparingly, only for things that must always exist, such as the spawn or entrance. In client code, don't assume parts exist: use WaitForChild or ChildAdded/streaming events and nil checks. For memory: lower StreamingTargetRadius (and keep StreamingMinRadius small) so less is kept around the player; use StreamOutBehavior = Opportunistic so far content streams out; avoid Persistent models; and use ModelStreamingMode = Atomic or LevelOfDetail = StreamingMesh for distant models so they show low-detail imposters. Profile with the Developer Console memory tab and test with device emulation.
C21:
The Input Action System is instance-based: an InputContext (enabled/disabled, with Priority and Sink) holds InputAction instances (a named action with a Type: Bool, Direction1D/2D/3D, ViewportPosition). Each InputAction holds InputBinding children that map devices to it (KeyCode such as LeftShift, gamepad ButtonL3, touch UI buttons via UIButton, plus composites like Up/Down/Left/Right for directions). Put the context where the client can see it (for example in StarterGui, StarterPlayerScripts or ReplicatedStorage, consumed by a LocalScript). Reading Sprint:
```lua
local ctx = script.Parent:WaitForChild("GameplayContext")
local sprint = ctx:WaitForChild("Sprint") -- InputAction, Type = Bool
sprint.Pressed:Connect(function() humanoid.WalkSpeed = 24 end)
sprint.Released:Connect(function() humanoid.WalkSpeed = 16 end)
-- or poll: local held = sprint:GetState()
-- sprint.StateChanged:Connect(function(state) ... end)
```
Toggle the context's Enabled flag to switch control schemes (menus, vehicles), and use Priority/Sink to resolve conflicts. Rebinding means changing the bindings' KeyCode. In 2026 Roblox moved the default PlayerModule (character movement, jump and camera controls) onto the Input Action System, so default controls are exposed as IAS contexts and actions you can rebind or disable instead of forking ControlModule. Forked or legacy PlayerScripts and ContextActionService code may need review. I'm not certain of the exact rollout details, so check the current announcement.
